entities.name: Mitochondrial EF-G
observations: The 761-aa query sequence exactly matches curated UniProt reference B9W9T4 from Candida dubliniensis; molecular mass is 84,343 Da and theoretical pI is 5.92.
Curated homologs identify it as a mitochondrial GTPase and translation elongation factor that catalyzes GTP-dependent ribosomal translocation.
Pfam domains support an EF-G architecture: GTP_EFTU at residues 67–345, EF-G domain II around 376–454, EFG_III at 469–542, EFG_IV at 543–660, and EFG_C at 663–748.
The N-terminal region is consistent with a mitochondrial targeting peptide; the curated reference assigns residues 1–33 as a mitochondrial transit peptide and residues 34–761 as the mature chain.
Sequence-based properties: instability index 38.7, GRAVY -0.31, aromaticity 0.068, estimated charge at pH 7 of -10.1.
Curated GO annotations include mitochondrial localization, GTP binding, GTPase activity, translation elongation factor activity, and mitochondrial translational elongation.

entities.name: Mitochondrial translation elongation
observations: Mitochondrial EF-G functions in protein biosynthesis by driving the elongation-stage ribosomal translocation step.
The factor promotes movement of A-site peptidyl-tRNA and P-site deacylated tRNA to the P and E sites, respectively, with coupled mRNA and ribosome conformational changes.
